Task: Draft a complete business plan for a hypothetical coffee shop.

Brewed Awakening Café  
Comprehensive Business Plan  
Prepared: [Month Year]

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Executive Summary
────────────────────────────────────────
Brewed Awakening Café (BAC) will be a 60-seat, urban-chic coffee shop located in the revitalized Riverfront Arts District of Portland, Oregon. Our mission is “to awaken community through ethically sourced coffee, inclusive space, and creative expression.” We will differentiate through:

• 100 % fair-trade, single-origin coffees roasted in-house   
• Plant-forward, locally sourced pastries & light fare  
• Immersive “coffee education” classes and tasting flights  
• Rotating gallery walls for local artists and weekly live music  

Seeking a total investment of $275,000—$125,000 owner equity, $150,000 SBA-backed term loan—BAC projects year-one revenue of $640,000 with a 63 % gross margin and breakeven at month 10.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Company Description
────────────────────────────────────────
Legal Form     : Oregon LLC  
Opening Date    : April 1, 2025  
Location      : 143 Riverfront Blvd., Portland, OR  
Vision       : Become the neighborhood’s “third place,” fusing specialty coffee with community arts.  
Values       : Sustainability, Transparency, Equity, Creativity, Hospitality.  

Goals (3-year)  
• Achieve $1.1 M annual sales with 12 % net profit.  
• Roast 60 % of beans in-house and launch a small e-commerce line.  
• Donate 3 % of profits to local arts nonprofits.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Market Analysis
────────────────────────────────────────
Industry Overview  
• US coffee shop market size 2024: $49 B; CAGR 4.5 %.  
• Specialty segment growing faster at 8 %. Consumers pay premiums for craft and ethics.

Target Market Segments (Riverfront radius 1.5 mi, pop. 27,000)  
1. Remote professionals (ages 25-45; weekday AM/PM; value Wi-Fi, ambiance).  
2. Art & culture enthusiasts (ages 21-55; evening events).  
3. Eco-conscious consumers (all ages; pay extra for sustainable sourcing).  

Competitive Landscape  
Within 1-mile: 4 independents, 2 chains. Gaps: in-house roasting, evening programming. Largest chain (Starbucks) emphasizes speed, not experience. Opportunity: curated, community-based positioning.

SWOT  
Strengths : Owner’s 10 yr roasting experience, strong supplier network.  
Weaknesses: New brand awareness.  
Opportunities: Growth of remote work; “third place” demand.  
Threats  : Rising lease rates; commodity coffee price volatility.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Organization & Management
────────────────────────────────────────
Owners  
• Alex Chen – Managing Member/Head Roaster (60 % equity)  
• Maya Patel – Operations & Community Director (40 % equity)

Key Staff (Year 1)  
• Café Manager (1)  
• Lead Baristas (2)  
• Baristas (6 PT = 3 FTE)  
• Kitchen Prep/Baker (1)  
• Marketing & Events Coordinator (0.5 FTE)  
Legal/Advisory: CPA firm, employment attorney, SBA mentor board.

Org Chart  
Members → Café Manager → Baristas & Kitchen  
    → Marketing/Events  

HR & Culture  
• Livable wage $20 /hr + tips.  
• Health stipend for FT, commuter benefits, paid volunteer days.  
• Quarterly training on sensory, latte art, DEI.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. Service & Product Line
────────────────────────────────────────
Coffee & Beverages  
• Espresso classics ($3-$5)  
• Single-origin pour-overs ($5-$7)  
• Seasonal signature drinks (e.g., Lavender-Honey Oat Latte $6)  
• Nitro cold brew on tap ($5)  
• Loose-leaf teas, kombucha, craft sodas.

Food  
• House-baked pastries (gluten-free & vegan options).  
• Toast & grain bowls, panini, seasonal soups (avg. $8).  
• Weekend brunch specials.

Retail  
• 12-oz bags of in-house roasted beans ($17-$22).  
• Branded merchandise (tumblers, tees).  
• Coffee class tickets ($40) and private cuppings.

Sourcing  
• Partnerships with Crop to Cup, Café Imports.  
• 100 % traceable beans; 1 % for Carbon offset.  
• Produce from four local farms, bread from Sunrise Bakery.

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Marketing & Sales Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
Brand Positioning: “Where coffee meets culture.”  
Channels & Tactics  
• Pre-launch: Pop-up tasting cart at Saturday Market; Instagram teaser campaign; local press preview.  
• Digital: SEO-optimized website with online ordering; Instagram, TikTok, monthly newsletter (2,500 subscribers goal Y1).  
• Loyalty: App-based rewards (Square) – buy 10, get 1 free; birthday drink.  
• Community: Art openings every First Friday; open-mic nights; sponsor Riverfront Clean-Up.  
• Collaboration: “Guest Roaster” events & beer-coffee collabs with nearby microbrewery.

Sales Mix Targets Y1  
Beverages 60 % | Food 25 % | Retail 10 % | Classes/Events 5 %

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Operations Plan
────────────────────────────────────────
Hours   : 6 AM–8 PM Mon-Thu; 6 AM–10 PM Fri-Sat; 7 AM–6 PM Sun.  
Square Footage: 2,100 sq ft (1,500 front-of-house; 350 roasting; 250 kitchen).  
Technology: La Marzocco Linea PB; Diedrich IR-12 roaster; Square POS; Toast Kitchen Display; Wi-Fi 1 Gb.  
Supply Chain: Weekly green-coffee deliveries; produce tri-weekly; backup distributors for dairy/non-dairy.  
Sustainability: Reusable cup discount, compostable cups/lids, spent-grounds partnership with local gardeners.

────────────────────────────────────────
8. Funding Request
────────────────────────────────────────
Total Project Cost $275,000  
• Build-out & Leasehold improvements     $115,000  
• Equipment & Furniture                  $85,000  
• Opening Inventory & Supplies           $18,000  
• Licenses, Insurance, Deposits          $12,000  
• Working Capital (6 mo)                 $45,000  

Financing Structure  
• Owner Equity             $125,000 (cash & sweat)  
• SBA 7(a) Loan            $150,000 @ 8.25 % APR, 10-yr amort.  

Use of Funds: Complete space renovation, acquire roaster & espresso setup, initial payroll, marketing rollout.

────────────────────────────────────────
9. Financial Projections
────────────────────────────────────────
Key Assumptions  
• Average ticket: $8.25; 140 daily transactions weekday, 200 weekend.  
• COGS: Beverages 32 %, Food 42 %, Retail 50 %.  
• Payroll incl. taxes/benefits: 31 % of sales.  
• Rent: $5,200/mo + NNN.  
• Yearly growth 12 % rev, 1 % cost inflation.

Income Statement (Summary)  
         Year 1 Year 2 Year 3  
Revenue    $640k $717k $803k  
Gross Profit $402k $462k $522k  
EBITDA    $58k  $88k  $115k  
Net Profit %  5.2 %  8.1 %  10.1 %  

Cash Flow: Positive month 10; YE 1 cash balance $32k.  
Breakeven: $54k monthly sales (avg 210 daily tickets).  
Sensitivity: +10 % COGS lowers net margin by 2 pts; 5 % rise in traffic offsets.

────────────────────────────────────────
10. Risk Analysis & Mitigation
────────────────────────────────────────
Risk     Mitigation  
Commodity price spikes  Forward contracts; menu price flexibility.  
Labor shortages     Training pipeline with local barista school; wage premium.  
Economic downturn   Expand retail/online sales; cost control.  
Regulatory (COVID-like) Diversify revenue via packaged beans & virtual classes.  

────────────────────────────────────────
11. Exit Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
• 5-year option to open second location or franchise.  
• Potential sale to regional micro-chain at 4-5× EBITDA.  
• Owners repay SBA loan from free cash flow; maintain lean balance sheet.

────────────────────────────────────────
12. Appendix
────────────────────────────────────────
A. Floor plan renderings  
B. Resumes of founders  
C. Letters of intent from suppliers & artists  
D. Detailed 36-month financial model (Excel)  
E. Market survey data of 512 local respondents  
F. Environmental impact assessment summary

────────────────────────────────────────
